title: VirusCascade: Hijacking Collaborative Reflection in LLM-Powered Recommender Agents
abstract: arXiv:2609.38270v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Advancing beyond traditional static scoring models, LLM-powered agentic recommender systems (LLM-ARS) instantiate users and items as autonomous agents, whose semantic states are dynamically refined through a recurrent process known as collaborative reflection. While this mechanism improves recommendation quality, it simultaneously introduces a systemic vulnerability: adversarial evidence injected into a single agent can be rationalised into a legitimate preference narrative, written back into memory, and propagated to other agents through interaction contexts. We term the local rationalisation process reflection laundering, and its system-wide escalation through collaborative reflection collaborative-reflection hijacking. translated_title: VirusCascade：劫持基于大语言模型的推荐智能体中的协同反思
translated_abstract: 超越传统的静态评分模型，基于大语言模型的智能体推荐系统（LLM-ARS）将用户和物品实例化为自主智能体，其语义状态通过一种被称为“协同反思”的循环过程进行动态优化。虽然这一机制提升了推荐质量，但同时也引入了一种系统性漏洞：注入到单个智能体中的对抗性证据可以被合理化为合法的偏好叙事，写回记忆，并通过交互上下文传播给其他智能体。我们将这种局部合理化过程称为“反思洗白”，将其通过协同反思在系统范围内的升级称为“协同反思劫持”。现有的推荐系统攻击，无论是基于交互级数据投毒还是文本级对抗扰动，都假设静态流水线，因而无法利用这种循环式的多智能体放大机制。
tldr: 本文揭示了基于大语言模型的智能体推荐系统中的新型安全漏洞，提出VirusCascade攻击方法，通过“反思洗白”将注入单个智能体的对抗性证据合理化，并借助协同反思机制在多智能体间传播放大，实现对整个推荐系统的劫持。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals a novel security vulnerability in LLM-powered agentic recommender systems and proposes VirusCascade, an attack that rationalizes adversarial evidence injected into a single agent ("reflection laundering") and amplifies it system-wide through collaborative reflection ("collaborative-reflection hijacking").
